notes: Sourced from DirectOut's official EXBOX.MD User's Manual Version 1.8 (Nov 2023), mirrored from the manufacturer's own download link at directout.eu/download/manual-exbox-md/, and cross-checked against the manufacturer product page directout.eu/product/exbox-md/. Port names taken verbatim from the manual's rear-panel labeling tables (Chapter 4: Global Control / Input-Output MADI / Input-Output Network) and Chapter 7 Technical Data / Appendix A. Desktop/modular unit (140 x 42 x 146 mm, 1/3 of 19in rack width) - not assigned rackUnits since it is not a standard full-width rack chassis; DirectOut sells an optional BOXMOUNT.XL kit that fits up to three EXBOX units side-by-side into 1U. Connector mapping caveats: (1) MADI SC ports use an SC-type fiber connector (ISO/IEC 9314-3 FDDI, 1310nm, multimode 62.5/125 or 50/125); SC is not in the allowed connector enum, so it was mapped to the closest available fiber option, fiber-lc - the physical connector on the device is SC, not LC. (2) The two power inputs (PSU 1/PSU 2) are Hirose HR10 4-pin circular locking DC connectors (9-24V DC, 2.5A max, pins: 1=DC+, 2=DC+, 3=DC-, 4=DC-); mapped to xlr4-dc as the closest 4-pin locking DC connector in the allowed list, though it is a Hirose HR10, not an XLR-bodied connector. (3) Grade was intentionally omitted on the MADI BNC ports: although BNC ports normally take the sdi-* grade scale, these carry MADI (AES10) signal, not SDI, so applying an SDI grade would misrepresent the signal type; the manual's own MADI-specific specs (56/64 channel, 48k/96k frame format) don't map to any allowed grade enum. (4) Network ports are confirmed Gigabit Ethernet (1000 Mbit/s) explicitly stated in Technical Data as "Gigabit Ethernet", supporting Dante and AES67 audio-over-IP, not general-purpose data networking. (5) Device also supports PTP (IEEE 1588-2002) clocking over the network ports, and BNC IN can double as an AES11 word-clock input - these are protocol/clocking details, not separate physical ports. No dedicated on/off power switch exists; device powers on immediately when any valid PSU or PoE source is connected.

ports.name: MADI BNC IN
ports.note: MADI (AES10) coaxial input, 75 ohm; may alternatively be used as AES11 word-clock input

ports.name: MADI SC OUT
ports.note: Optical MADI output on SC-type multimode fiber connector (62.5/125 or 50/125, 1310nm); SC is not in the allowed connector list so fiber-lc was chosen as the closest optical-fiber match. Single-mode SC available on request per manufacturer.

ports.name: MADI SC IN
ports.note: Optical MADI input on SC-type multimode fiber connector; SC not in allowed list, mapped to fiber-lc as closest fiber connector.

ports.name: MADI SFP I/O
ports.note: Empty SFP cage; ships without transceiver module, user must fit their own MADI SFP module

ports.name: 01 (PoE)
ports.note: Gigabit Ethernet Dante/AES67 network port; also accepts PoE (Class 0, 0.4-13W, IEEE 802.3af) for device power

ports.name: PSU 1
ports.note: Hirose HR10 4-pin locking DC socket, 9-24V DC, external power supply; closest allowed connector to Hirose HR10 4-pin (2 pins DC+, 2 pins DC-)

ports.name: PSU 2
ports.note: Second redundant Hirose HR10 4-pin DC input, 9-24V DC; unit operates on a single PSU, second is for redundancy
